title: Fencing: specialty-scoped contractor identity with perimeter-work exclusions
hypothesis: An active fencing-specialty contractor record can establish a business and principal or license-role candidate, but its published phone is only a business-contact candidate. An owner-confirmed mobile requires separate owner evidence plus mobile, live, DNC, suppression, and delivery-dedupe gates.
ownerSource: Legally eligible contractor registers with an explicit fencing specialty: WA L&I active FENC rows and CA CSLB C-13 master/personnel records. A WA primary principal or CSLB personnel title is candidate role evidence, not ownership confirmation.
phoneSource: A published register business phone, contrasted with the current Maps business listing when permitted. It remains a business or candidate contact until exclusivity, mobile, live, DNC, global suppression/dedupe, and independent owner-evidence gates pass.

workflow.label: State legal gate
workflow.detail: Allow only a legally eligible public contractor-register route; keep restricted or unavailable register routes out of intake.

workflow.label: Active fencing-specialty register
workflow.detail: Require an active explicit fencing classification such as WA FENC or CA C-13; do not treat generic construction registration as fencing evidence.

workflow.label: Permitted fencing listing fallback
workflow.detail: Use the live Maps fence-contractor route only where a register route is unavailable or not yet implemented and the fallback is permitted.

workflow.label: Hold restricted source
workflow.detail: Do not ingest prohibited or commercially restricted list sources.

workflow.label: Fencing and operator-fit filter
workflow.detail: Require fencing installation or repair evidence; reject materials retail, temporary construction fencing, security-perimeter integrators, railings, gates-only, decks, landscaping-only, franchise, stale, and multi-location matches.

workflow.label: Hold off-segment candidate
workflow.detail: Do not convert an adjacent trade or commercial perimeter supplier into an independent fencing-owner candidate.

workflow.label: Owner-role assessment
workflow.detail: Retain an Individual entity, Sole Owner, partner, or member as stronger candidate evidence; principal, qualifier, RMO, RME, officer, or corporate role needs independent owner evidence.

workflow.label: Hold unsupported role
workflow.detail: Do not label a qualifier, employee, corporate officer, or unsupported principal as the business owner.

workflow.label: Candidate contact contrast
workflow.detail: Compare a published register and Maps number where both exist; missing, shared, duplicate, or office-only numbers do not become direct owner contacts.

workflow.label: Hold unsupported contact
workflow.detail: Do not infer a private mobile or call a public business line an owner handset.

workflow.label: Contact and compliance gates
workflow.detail: Apply mobile line type, live status, DNC, global suppression/dedupe, and independent owner-evidence checks.

workflow.label: Hold failed verification
workflow.detail: Park non-mobile, unreachable, suppressed, shared, or ownership-unsupported cases.

workflow.label: Deliver supported classification
workflow.detail: Deliver only after every required gate passes; owner-confirmed mobile requires independent owner evidence.

edges.label: retail, temporary, perimeter, adjacent, brand, or stale
all contact and owner-evidence gates pass
line, compliance, dedupe, or owner-evidence failure

failures.risk: The live Maps-first fence-contractor route begins with an advertised business line rather than trade-scoped identity.
failures.mitigation: Use a legally eligible FENC/C-13 record as trade and candidate-role evidence, then use Maps as contrast or permitted fallback.

failures.risk: CA C-13 and WA FENC classifications cannot be selected from ingested rows because the adapters do not persist specialty/classification into the field consumed by register-source filters.
failures.mitigation: Persist normalized classifications in a filterable trade field, or implement source-specific class filtering before adding fencing register mappings.

failures.risk: Fence supply yards, temporary construction fencing, commercial perimeter/security installers, gates-only businesses, railings, decks, and landscaping enter the independent fencing route.
failures.mitigation: Require installation or repair fit and explicitly hold those segments until separately approved.

failures.risk: A principal, qualifier, or public office line is represented as an owner-confirmed mobile.
failures.mitigation: Preserve source role and phone provenance; require contact, compliance, and independent owner-evidence gates.

failures.risk: Texas and North Carolina are treated as statewide fencing-license routes although the catalog marks fencing unlicensed statewide there.
failures.mitigation: Do not fabricate a statewide fencing-register path; use only a permitted business-listing fallback or a separately reviewed local route.

iterations.hypothesis: A free, active fencing-specialty register can contribute trade and candidate-contact coverage before any owner classification.
iterations.test: Aggregate-only live query of 20 WA L&I rows on 2026-09-24 where statuscode was A and specialtycode1desc contained FENC.
iterations.observed: 20/20 rows were active and had specialty, primary principal, and published-phone fields; 6/20 were Individual business entities. The observation establishes field coverage only, not owner role, handset ownership, mobile status, reachability, DNC, or delivery.
iterations.change: Use an explicit specialty branch and role/contact holds. Do not treat the principal or published phone as owner-confirmed; first repair class persistence so the current runtime can select fencing rows.

measurement.result: WA L&I m8qx-ubtq active rows whose specialtycode1desc contained FENC: 20/20 active, 20/20 specialty present, 20/20 primaryprincipalname present, 20/20 phonenumber present, and 6/20 businesstypecodedesc = Individual. Aggregate-only observation; no names, phones, addresses, license numbers, or business names retained. It does not measure mobile status, reachability, DNC, ownership confirmation, handset ownership, or delivery.

cost.note: No clean delivered owner contact was measured. Historical fencing brain rates use a different denominator and are not a per-clean cost for this workflow.

implementation.summary: The live recipe-A fencing discovery and generic relevance classifier exist, and WA/CA contractor adapters are present. Fencing has no register-source mapping, and the adapters do not retain FENC/C-13 classification in the field used by pullNames filtering, so no specialty-scoped fencing register route can run today.

nextMeasurement: Add synthetic WA FENC and non-FENC rows plus CA C-13 and non-C-13 master/personnel rows. Verify a fencing job selects only the explicit fencing class, preserves principal/personnel as candidate-role evidence, holds retail/perimeter/temporary/adjacent listings, and cannot deliver an owner-confirmed contact without independent evidence. After authorization, measure mobile, live, DNC-cleared, reached-owner, and delivered outcomes with separate denominators.
